lines.japanese: 今日もいつもの場所に停まっていたピンクのミニバン。
lines.english: The pink minivan was parked in its usual spot again today.

lines.japanese: 店の前に覚えのある小さな制服の背中が見えて、思わず俺は立ちどまった。
lines.english: I spotted a familiar little figure in uniform outside the shop and stopped without thinking.

lines.japanese: いや、なんでだよ。べつに止まる必要ねーじゃんよ。
lines.english: Wait, why the hell had I stopped? I had no reason to stop.

lines.japanese: すぐに俺は歩きだした、歩きながら首を鳴らした、首を鳴らしながら頬の裏を突いた。なめんな。
lines.english: I started walking again at once. As I walked, I cracked my neck. As I cracked my neck, I prodded the inside of my cheek. Don't underestimate me.

lines.japanese: 「うーっす」
lines.english: “Yo.”

lines.japanese: 四角いピンクのミニバンに近付きながら、俺はことさら気だるげな挨拶を放りなげた。車内の店主より先に、クレープを手にした制服の客が振りかえった。
lines.english: As I approached the boxy pink minivan, I tossed out a greeting of studied weariness. Before the owner inside could answer, the uniformed customer holding a crêpe turned around.
“Ah.”

lines.japanese: そいつは俺の顔を見て口を丸く開けたが──
lines.english: Her mouth rounded into an O when she saw my face—

lines.japanese: ──へこっと音もなく会釈した弾みにその表情をほころばせた。
lines.english: —then softened into a smile as she bobbed her head in a tiny, silent bow.

lines.japanese: 俺はリアクションに困った。笑いかえすのが正解な気はしたけど、でも、そんなん俺のガラでもキャラでもないだろ。なめんな。
lines.english: I didn't know how to respond. Smiling back felt like the right answer, but that wasn't my style. It wasn't who I was. Don't underestimate me.

lines.japanese: 「どもー、ご無沙汰してます鳳ですー」
lines.english: “Hellooo. Long time no see. Otori here.”

lines.japanese: 「いや、覚えてるけど」
lines.english: “I remember you.”

lines.japanese: 「妹の方ですー」
lines.english: “The younger sister.”

lines.japanese: 「いや、分かるけど」
lines.english: “I know.”

lines.japanese: 中一日を開けて再会したデコと締まりのない口が、なんだかやけに懐かしい。やっぱ俺は笑うべきなのか。
lines.english: After one whole day apart, that forehead and slack mouth already looked weirdly nostalgic. Was I supposed to smile after all?

lines.japanese: 「なめんな」
lines.english: “Don’t underestimate me.”

lines.japanese: 目潰しピースを突きつけて、ちょっとニヒルな微笑み返し。俺にしちゃ上出来だろ。
lines.english: I thrust the Eye-Gouging Peace Sign at her and answered with a faintly cynical smile. Pretty good, by my standards.

lines.japanese: 「やー、また会ってしまいましたねー。はー、実に奇遇ですねー」
lines.english: “Well, look at that—we meet again. What an incredible coincidence.”

lines.japanese: 鳴は八重歯を覗かせていた。奇遇という言葉にはあまり現実味がなかった。
lines.english: Naru showed her little fang. The word *coincidence* did not sound terribly convincing.

lines.japanese: 「あー、まー……」
lines.english: “Yeah, well...”

lines.japanese: 俺はふた又の槍を下ろし、曖昧に頷きながらやつのクレープに目を落とした。
lines.english: I lowered my two-pronged spear and nodded vaguely, letting my eyes drop to her crêpe.

lines.japanese: 「お、おお。なにおまえ、美味そうなの食ってんじゃん」
lines.english: “Oh, hey. That looks good.”

lines.japanese: 「一口いりますかー？」
lines.english: “Would you like a bite?”

lines.japanese: 「え……あァ、いや、いいや」
lines.english: “What...? Nah, I'm good.”

lines.japanese: 俺は小娘と食いかけのクレープから目を外して、なにか他のもの──ええと、パル姐さんの姿を探した。そうだよ。あの店員、なんで出てこないんだよ。
lines.english: I tore my eyes from the kid and her half-eaten crêpe and looked for something else—uh, Paru. Right. Why wasn't the woman behind the counter coming out?

lines.japanese: 「パルさん」
lines.english: “Paru.”

lines.japanese: カウンターから首を突っこんで中を覗く。
lines.english: I stuck my head through the service window and peered inside.

lines.japanese: 「なんだよ、忙しいの」
lines.english: “What, are you busy?”

lines.japanese: しかし腕組みしたクレープ屋は、暇そうに調理台へ腰を預けて薄ら笑いを浮かべていた。
lines.english: But the crêpe seller stood with her arms folded, leaning idly against the prep counter with a thin smile.

lines.japanese: 「おいおい、用もないのにいちいちお姉ちゃん呼ぶんじゃないよ。まったく、肝の小さい弟だねぇどうも」
lines.english: “Now, now. Don’t call your big sister over every time you’ve got nothing to say. What a fainthearted little brother you are.”

lines.japanese: 「あァ？　んだコラ、俺の肝臓見たことあんのかコラ。レントゲン医かてめえは。上等だちょっと待ってろ、いま金具付きブラジャー外すからコノヤロウ」
lines.english: “Huh? You ever seen the size of my liver, asshole? What are you, an X-ray tech? Fine, bring it on. Just wait while I take off my underwire bra.”

lines.japanese: 「はー、ドラさん肝臓小さいんですか？」
lines.english: “Oh. Is your liver small, Dora?”

lines.japanese: 「馬鹿おめ、小さくねえっつうの。俺のレバーはボリュームたっぷりファミリーサイズだっつうの。鉄分たっぷり、とってもヘルシーだっつうの。ていうか、あれ、この流れ前にやんなかったっけ」
lines.english: “Idiot, I said it's not small. My liver's a great big family-size slab. Packed with iron and ever so healthy. Wait—haven't we done this routine before?”

lines.japanese: 「あたしに聞くなよ」
lines.english: “Don’t ask me.”

lines.japanese: 「どっちに聞いたっていいじゃねーか。つか、なあ、この小娘ここで何してんの？」
lines.english: “I can ask whoever I want. Anyway, what's this kid doing here?”

lines.japanese: 「あたしに聞くなってんだよ」
lines.english: “I said don’t ask me.”

lines.japanese: 「ストロベリーヨーグルトに舌鼓を打ってますよー」
lines.english: “I'm savoring a strawberry-yogurt crêpe.”

lines.japanese: 「あ？　ああ……ああ、そう」
lines.english: “Huh? Oh... Right.”

lines.japanese: 俺はカウンターに頭を突っ込んだまま、背後に立つ小娘を肩越しに振りかえった。パルさんは意地悪く背中を向けて、どうでも良さげな棚の整理を始めた。
lines.english: With my head still inside the window, I looked back over my shoulder at the kid behind me. Paru spitefully turned her back and began tidying a shelf that plainly did not need it.

lines.japanese: 今日もパルクレープのＢＧＭは、バブル末期を席捲したハイパー・ディスコチューン。腰振りダンスと共に現れて消えていった、前世紀の無形文化遺産だ。
lines.english: Today's music at Paru Crêpes was another hyper-disco tune that had conquered the dying years of the bubble economy: an intangible cultural treasure of the last century, born and buried with a hip-swinging dance.

lines.japanese: サンプリングされた女性コーラスが馬鹿みたいにフゥフゥはしゃいでるのを、俺たちは否応なしに受けいれていた。
lines.english: We had no choice but to endure the sampled female chorus whooping away like idiots.

lines.japanese: フゥフゥが終わったと思ったら、今度はフゥワ！フゥワ！が始まった。
lines.english: The whoo-whoo ended. Then the whoo-wah, whoo-wah began.

lines.japanese: フゥワ！　フゥワ！
lines.english: Whoo-wah! Whoo-wah!

lines.japanese: フゥワ！　フゥワ！
lines.english: Whoo-wah! Whoo-wah!

lines.japanese: 「……あのさ」
「はいっ」
lines.english: “Yes!”

lines.japanese: 「あー、の……ほらアレ、チャリンコ。そう、チャリンコ。おまえチャリンコ見つかったの」
lines.english: “Uh... You know. The bike. Yeah, your bike. Did you find it?”

lines.japanese: 「あー、えー、あんまり見つかってないですねー」
lines.english: “Well, um, it isn't very found yet.”

lines.japanese: 「なに、あんまりって。あんまりとかたんまりとか、程度の差あんの」
lines.english: “What do you mean, not very? Are there degrees of found? A little found, a whole lot found?”

lines.japanese: 「あー、えー、あんまりないんですけどー」
lines.english: “Well, um, there hasn't been much finding...”

lines.japanese: 「ふーん」
lines.english: “Huh.”

lines.japanese: フゥワ！　フゥワ！　フゥワ！　フゥワ！　イェ──ッ！
lines.english: Whoo-wah! Whoo-wah! Whoo-wah! Whoo-wah! Yeeeah!

lines.japanese: うるせーばか、イェーじゃねえよクソ歌。
lines.english: Shut the hell up. Don't you yeeah at me, you shitty song.

lines.japanese: 鳴は分け目でも気になるのか、落ちつきなく両手の指先で前髪を梳いていた。
lines.english: Maybe Naru was worried about the part in her hair. She restlessly combed her bangs with the fingertips of both hands.

lines.japanese: 「パルさん」
lines.english: “Paru.”

lines.japanese: 俺はまたバンの中に呼びかけた。
lines.english: I called into the van again.

lines.japanese: 「あんさ、今日なんか俺に仕事来てないの。エージ以外で」
lines.english: “You got any work for me today? Anyone but Eiji.”

lines.japanese: 「来てるよ」
lines.english: “Sure do.”

lines.japanese: 仲介人はしれっと答えた。
lines.english: The broker answered without a flicker.

lines.japanese: 「は？　マジ？　エージ以外でだよ」
lines.english: “What? Seriously? I said anyone but Eiji.”

lines.japanese: 「おう。田村さんとこの事務所の、配置換えの手伝いさ」
lines.english: “Yeah. Tamura's office needs help changing its layout.”

lines.japanese: 「マジかよ。そういうの先に言えよ。あそこチップくれんだよ」
lines.english: “Seriously? Lead with that. Those people tip.”

lines.japanese: 全米が痩せた、という煽り文句でプチヒットを飛ばした、健康食品の販売会社。苦情電話の絶えない事務所だったが、社長は消費者にお見せできないほど気前が良かった。
lines.english: The health-food company had scored a minor hit with the slogan ALL AMERICA LOST WEIGHT. Complaints never stopped coming into the office, but the president was more generous than they could ever let the customers find out.

lines.japanese: 「パルさん、ソレいつだって」
lines.english: “Paru, when's the job?”

lines.japanese: 「明日の夜８時半に来てほしいってさ」
lines.english: “They want you there at eight-thirty tomorrow night.”

lines.japanese: 明日の夜８時半。
lines.english: Eight-thirty tomorrow night.

lines.japanese: 俺は身を乗りだして、車内に貼られていた擬人化黒ネズミのカレンダーを覗きこんだ。明日は金曜日。ってことは、俺が≪コックピット≫に入るのは１０時から──
lines.english: I leaned in to inspect the calendar taped up inside the van, decorated with an anthropomorphic black mouse. Tomorrow was Friday. That meant I entered the *Cockpit* at ten—

lines.japanese: ──ああごめん、こっちの話。おまえには分からないだろうから、いまのは軽く聞きながしてくれ。
lines.english: —oh, sorry. I was talking to myself. You wouldn't understand, so just let that go in one ear and out the other.

lines.japanese: 「８時半、無理だな……１０時半とかにしてもらえねーかな」
lines.english: “Eight-thirty won't work... Think they could move it to ten-thirty?”

lines.japanese: 「なんか用事あんの？」
lines.english: “You got plans?”

lines.japanese: 「さあ。知らねーけど、約束してっから」
lines.english: “Hell if I know. I promised somebody, though.”

lines.japanese: 「誰と？」
lines.english: “Who?”

lines.japanese: 「パルさんの知らないやつ」
lines.english: “Somebody you don't know.”

lines.japanese: 「ふーん」
lines.english: “Hmm.”

lines.japanese: 俺が詮索してほしくないのを、パル姐さんは読みとってくれたみたいだ。つまらなそうに呟いて、ストラップだらけの携帯電話を開いた。
lines.english: Paru seemed to understand that I didn't want her prying. She muttered without interest and flipped open her phone, festooned with straps.

lines.japanese: 「１０時半だね。聞いてやるからちょっと待ってな」
lines.english: “Ten-thirty, right? I'll ask them. Hold on.”

lines.japanese: 「さんきゅ」
lines.english: “Thanks.”

lines.japanese: 女が電話を耳に当てる。俺はカウンターから少し身を引いた。まあ、マナーとして一応。
lines.english: The woman put the phone to her ear. I stepped back from the counter a little. Basic manners, more or less.

lines.japanese: 鳴がその一部始終を見ていた。
lines.english: Naru had watched the entire exchange.

lines.japanese: 「はー、ドラさんいろんなお仕事されてるんですねー」
lines.english: “Wow. You do all sorts of work, Dora.”

lines.japanese: 「あー、まーな……ぶっちゃけ俺、遅刻とか無断欠勤多いから、ひとつンとこ長続きしねンだよ。あとアレ、いわゆる職場の付き合いっての苦手だし」
lines.english: “Yeah, well... Honestly, I’m late a lot and I no-show without calling, so I never last long anywhere. I’m no good at all the social stuff that comes with having coworkers, either.”

lines.japanese: 「はー」
lines.english: “Oh.”

lines.japanese: 小娘は息継ぎみたいな返事をした。俺の言葉が冗談なのか本気なのか、分かりにくかったのかもしれない。
lines.english: The kid answered as though taking a breath. Maybe she couldn't tell whether I was joking or serious.

lines.japanese: 「まあ、要するにアレ、おまえはこういうオトナになんなよって話」
lines.english: “Anyway, the point is: don't grow into this kind of adult.”

lines.japanese: 「はー、手遅れかもしれません」
lines.english: “Oh. It may already be too late.”
“Huh?”

lines.japanese: だらりと腕を垂らす、やつの制服姿を見下ろした。
lines.english: I looked down at her standing there in her uniform, arms hanging limp.

lines.japanese: あれ……制服？
lines.english: Wait... uniform?

lines.japanese: 「いや、おまえ偉いじゃん。休みの日にもガッコ行ってんじゃん」
lines.english: “No, you're doing great. Going to school even on a holiday.”

lines.japanese: そう、平日にさえバックレてる連中がうようよ存在するご時世だってのに。なあ森里。なあ香田。なあ以下略。
lines.english: And this in an age crawling with people who skip school even on weekdays. Right, Morisato? Koda? The list goes on.

lines.japanese: 「やー、ところがですねー。実はこれがそう誇れた話でもなくてですねー」
lines.english: “Well, you see... It isn't actually anything to be proud of.”

lines.japanese: 「ああ」
lines.english: “Ah.”

lines.japanese: つまりアレか、単なる補習か。鳴はお恥ずかしいとばかりに、ブレザーの襟を立てて臆病な亀みたいに首を縮めた。
lines.english: Ah. So: plain old remedial classes. As if to hide her shame, Naru turned up the collar of her blazer and drew in her neck like a timid turtle.

lines.japanese: 俺はその頭を鷲づかみして引っこぬきたくなったけど、パルさんに冷やかされそうだからやめておいた。
lines.english: I wanted to seize her head and pull it back out, but Paru would tease me, so I restrained myself.

lines.japanese: 「ドラぁ！　残念、１０時半じゃ遅いってさ」
lines.english: “Dora! Bad news. Ten-thirty’s too late.”

lines.japanese: 勢いよくケータイを閉じる音が聞こえた。俺は慌ててミニバンに近付いた。
lines.english: I heard the sharp snap of her phone closing. I hurried back to the minivan.

lines.japanese: 「そっか、やっぱだめか。ああ、じゃあ断わっといてくれたの」
lines.english: “Right. No dice after all. You turned them down for me, then?”

lines.japanese: パル姉さんの三角巾が縦に揺れた。
lines.english: Paru's kerchief bobbed up and down.

lines.japanese: 「そか。悪りぃね」
lines.english: “Got it. Sorry about that.”

lines.japanese: 俺は小さく頭を下げる。ツイてない。美味しい仕事だったのに、“全米が痩せた”。世の中ままならねー。
lines.english: I dipped my head. Rotten luck. It had been a sweet little job, and now *All America Lost Weight.* Nothing ever went the way you wanted.

lines.japanese: 気付いたらフゥワ！フゥワ！が、また頭から始まっていた。
lines.english: Before I knew it, the whoo-wah, whoo-wah had started again from the top.

lines.japanese: フゥワ！　フゥワ！
lines.english: Whoo-wah! Whoo-wah!

lines.japanese: いや、もうええっちゅーの。
lines.english: Oh, enough already.

lines.japanese: 「あー……じゃあまあ、そろそろ行くわ俺」
lines.english: “Well... I should get going.”

lines.japanese: 「えっ、もう？」
lines.english: “What? Already?”

lines.japanese: そりゃ俺はプーだけど、繁華街の端でぼけっと懐メロに浸ってるほどには暇じゃない。と思うよ。
lines.english: Sure, I was unemployed, but I wasn't so idle that I could stand around at the edge of the entertainment district basking in old pop songs. Or so I liked to think.

lines.japanese: 「そんじゃな。えーと、なめんな？」
lines.english: “See you. Uh... Don't underestimate me?”

lines.japanese: 俺は別れの目潰しピースをふたりへ向けた。
lines.english: I aimed a farewell Eye-Gouging Peace Sign at them both.

lines.japanese: 「はあ……えーと、なめんな？」
lines.english: “Oh... Um, don't underestimate me?”

lines.japanese: きょとんとした鳴が、出来の悪いパラパラ漫画みたいな動きで俺オリジナルのハンドサインを真似した。
lines.english: Looking blank, Naru copied my original hand sign in the stiff little jerks of a badly made flipbook.

lines.japanese: 「ドラ、ちょっと待った」
lines.english: “Dora, hold on.”

lines.japanese: 二本指を向けあう俺たちの横から、クレープ屋が窓枠を掴んで三角巾の顔を突きだした。
lines.english: From the side, as Naru and I stood pointing two fingers at each other, the crêpe seller gripped the window frame and stuck out her kerchief-wrapped head.

lines.japanese: 「なに」
lines.english: “What?”

lines.japanese: 「たまにゃ食ってくかい？　今日はおごってやるよ」
lines.english: “Why don't you have one for once? My treat today.”

lines.japanese: クレープ屋がくいっと顎を車内へ振った。景気のいい話。気味の悪い話。俺は上半身を横に倒してミニバンのフロントガラスを覗きこんだ。
lines.english: The crêpe seller jerked her chin toward the inside of the van. Now that was generous. Suspiciously generous. I leaned sideways and peered through the minivan's windshield.

lines.japanese: 「また鳥になんかクリーミィボムでも落とされたの」
lines.english: “Did another bird drop a creamy bomb on it or something?”

lines.japanese: 「あァ？　なに疑ってやんだこのガキゃ。あたしがそんな、見返りを求めるようなケチな女だってのかい」
lines.english: “Huh? What're you suspecting me for, you brat? You saying I'm some stingy woman who only gives when she wants something back?”

lines.japanese: 「経験談だっつーの。そっちも身に覚えあんだろが。ほら、おとといの夜だよ、覚えて──」
lines.english: “I'm speaking from experience. You know exactly what I'm talking about. The night before last, remember—”

lines.japanese: 「ガタガタがたがた文句ばっかり並べやがって七面倒くせえ！　ええッ、食ってくのか食ってかないのか、とっとと決めろってんだこのバカヤローが！」
lines.english: “Whine, whine, whine! Nothing but complaints, you almighty pain in the ass! Well? Are you eating or aren't you? Make up your goddamn mind, idiot!”

lines.japanese: ……なんだ。なんだこの状況。なんで俺が罵られてるんだ。食うか？　食えばいいのか？　ああ？
lines.english: ...What? What the hell was happening? Why was I getting yelled at? Was I supposed to eat? Was eating the right answer? Huh?

lines.japanese: しかし理由もないのに施しを受けていいのだろうか。俺はタダより高いものはないって言葉を知ってる。パル兄貴の言うとおり、たしかに可愛げのないガキだ。
lines.english: But was it right to accept charity for no reason? I knew the saying: nothing costs more than what comes free. Hardcase Paru was right. I really was an unlovable little bastard.
